Esophageal cancer: The patient's symptoms of increasing difficulty swallowing solid foods, regurgitation, and unintentional weight loss, along with the presence of a large polypoid pigmented lesion at 30 cm in the esophagus, are highly suggestive of esophageal cancer. The biopsy results showing an infiltrating malignant tumor with prominent nucleoli and cells in the submucosa and basal layer of the squamous mucosa further support this diagnosis.
Esophageal stricture: The patient's symptoms of difficulty swallowing solid foods and regurgitation could be caused by an esophageal stricture, which is a narrowing of the esophagus. However, the presence of a large polypoid pigmented lesion and the biopsy results showing malignant cells make esophageal cancer a more likely diagnosis.
